narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: John the seer on Patmos telling what he saw and heard, with his own exhortations to the reader.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lamb, the risen Lord, breaking into the vision with a sudden warning and blessing.

angel.name: Angel
angel.note: An angel of the vision: proclaiming with a loud voice, or explaining the vision to John.

a-voice-from-heaven.name: A voice from heaven
a-voice-from-heaven.note: An unnamed single voice from heaven, the temple, the throne or the altar; loud and solemn.

1.t: And I heard a great voice out of the temple, saying to the seven angels:
Go and pour out the seven vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.
1.q: great voice out of the temple, where no one but God can be (15:8): may be God himself

2.t: And the first went and poured out his vial upon the earth. And there fell a sore and grievous wound upon men who had the character of the beast: and upon them that adored the image thereof.

3.t: And the second angel poured out his vial upon the sea. And there came blood as it were of a dead man: and every living soul died in the sea.

4.t: And the third poured out his vial upon the rivers and the fountains of waters. And there was made blood.

5.t: And I heard the angel of the waters saying:
Thou art just, O Lord, who art and who wast, the Holy One, because thou hast judged these things.

6.t: For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets: and thou hast given them blood to drink. For they are worthy.

7.t: And I heard another, from the altar, saying:
Yea, O Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments.
7.q: "another, from the altar": an angel or the altar itself; taken as an unnamed voice from the altar

8.t: And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun. And it was given unto him to afflict men with heat and fire.

9.t: And men were scorched with great heat: and they blasphemed the name of God, who hath power over these plagues. Neither did they penance to give him glory.

10.t: And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast. And his kingdom became dark: and they gnawed their tongues for pain.

11.t: And they blasphemed the God of heaven, because of their pains and wounds: and did not penance for their works.

12.t: And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon that great river Euphrates and dried up the water thereof, that a way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun.

13.t: And I saw from the mouth of the dragon and from the mouth of the beast and from the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs.

14.t: For they are the spirits of devils, working signs: and they go forth unto the kings of the whole earth, to gather them to battle against the great day of the Almighty God.

15.t: Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.

16.t: And he shall gather them together into a place which in Hebrew is called Armagedon.

17.t: And the seventh angel poured out his vial upon the air. And there came a great voice out of the temple from the throne, saying:

17.q: voice from the throne, may be God himself (cf. 21:6)

18.t: And there were lightnings and voices and thunders: and there was a great earthquake, such an one as never had been since men were upon the earth, such an earthquake, so great.

19.t: And the great city was divided into three parts: and the cities of the Gentiles fell. And great Babylon came in remembrance before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the indignation of his wrath.

20.t: And every island fled away: and the mountains were not found.

21.t: And great hail, like a talent, came down from heaven upon men: and men blasphemed God, for the plague of the hail: because it was exceeding great.
